items.followUp: State one achievement of Schleiden and one achievement of Schwann.

rubric.why: Identifies Hooke’s observation of cells in cork.
rubric.description: Robert Hooke observed cork and named its tiny compartments “cells.”
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the observation of cork and identification or naming of cells.

rubric.why: Identifies Brown’s discovery of the nucleus.
rubric.description: Robert Brown discovered the nucleus in plant cells, including orchid cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that Brown discovered the nucleus.

modelAnswer: Robert Hooke observed tiny compartments in a slice of cork in 1665 and named them “cells.”
Robert Brown discovered the nucleus in plant cells in 1831.

rubric.why: Describes the material taken into the cell by phagocytosis.
rubric.description: Phagocytosis is the intake of solid particles by a cell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying solid particles as the material engulfed.

rubric.why: Describes the material taken into the cell by pinocytosis.
rubric.description: Pinocytosis is the intake of liquid droplets by a cell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying liquids or liquid droplets as the material taken in.

modelAnswer: In phagocytosis, a cell takes in solid particles by engulfing them.
In pinocytosis, a cell takes in liquid droplets.

items.followUp: What happens to enzyme activity when temperature rises above the optimum temperature?

rubric.why: Recognizes that enzyme activity depends on pH and that an optimum pH exists.
rubric.description: Each enzyme has an optimum pH at which it works fastest.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that each enzyme has a particular optimum pH.

rubric.why: Describes the effect of a pH change away from the optimum.
rubric.description: Moving away from the optimum pH decreases enzyme activity; an extreme pH may denature the enzyme.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that activity decreases away from the optimum or that extreme pH denatures the enzyme.

modelAnswer: Each enzyme works fastest at a particular optimum pH.
A change from the optimum pH decreases its activity; extreme pH may denature the enzyme.

items.followUp: Describe alcoholic fermentation and state its end products.

rubric.why: Identifies the substrate and anaerobic condition of lactic acid fermentation.
rubric.description: In the absence of oxygen, glucose is incompletely broken down during lactic acid fermentation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that glucose is broken down without oxygen.

rubric.why: Identifies the product and energy yield or the conversion to lactic acid.
rubric.description: The process forms lactic acid and releases a small amount of energy, about 2 ATP per glucose molecule.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming lactic acid as the product and indicating energy release or its formation from pyruvic acid.

modelAnswer: In the absence of oxygen, glucose is incompletely broken down in muscle cells or some bacteria.
It forms lactic acid and releases a small amount of energy (about 2 ATP per glucose molecule).

items.followUp: Explain how light intensity affects the rate of photosynthesis.

rubric.why: States the effect of increasing carbon dioxide concentration when it is limiting.
rubric.description: Increasing carbon dioxide concentration increases the rate of photosynthesis, provided other factors are not limiting.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking increased carbon dioxide concentration to an increased photosynthesis rate.

rubric.why: States that the increase in rate does not continue indefinitely.
rubric.description: The rate eventually levels off at a maximum when another factor becomes limiting.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the rate levels off or stops increasing at high carbon dioxide concentration.

modelAnswer: Increasing carbon dioxide concentration increases the rate of photosynthesis while carbon dioxide is a limiting factor.
At a high enough concentration, the rate levels off because another factor becomes limiting.

items.followUp: Define biology and describe the contributions of two Muslim scientists to biology.

rubric.why: Gives the meaning of biology.
rubric.description: Biology is the study of life or living organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition of biology.

rubric.why: Identifies a Muslim scientist’s contribution to the study of animals.
rubric.description: Abdul Malik Al-Asmai studied animals and wrote about them.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming Al-Asmai and describing his work on animals.

rubric.why: Identifies Ibn Sina’s medical contribution.
rubric.description: Ibn Sina was a famous physician and wrote Al-Qanun fit-Tibb, a major medical work.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming Ibn Sina and giving a relevant medical contribution.

rubric.why: Accepts a further relevant contribution by a Muslim scientist.
rubric.description: A relevant contribution by another Muslim scientist, such as Jabir bin Hayyan’s writings on animals or plants.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correctly named Muslim scientist with a relevant biological contribution.

modelAnswer: Biology is the study of life and living organisms.
Abdul Malik Al-Asmai studied animals and wrote books about them.
Ibn Sina was a famous physician and wrote Al-Qanun fit-Tibb, an important medical work.
Jabir bin Hayyan also wrote works on animals and plants.

items.followUp: Describe the structure and function of chromosomes in the nucleus.

rubric.why: Describes the membrane that encloses the nucleus.
rubric.description: The nucleus is surrounded by a nuclear membrane.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the nuclear membrane or envelope.

rubric.why: Identifies the material inside the nucleus.
rubric.description: The nucleus contains a fluid called nucleoplasm.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming nucleoplasm or describing the fluid inside the nucleus.

rubric.why: Identifies a component within the nucleus.
rubric.description: One or more nucleoli are present inside the nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the nucleolus.

rubric.why: Identifies the nuclear structures that carry hereditary material.
rubric.description: The nucleus contains chromosomes, which consist of chromatin when not dividing.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming chromosomes or chromatin.

rubric.why: States the nucleus’s control or hereditary role.
rubric.description: The nucleus controls cell activities and contains hereditary information in DNA and genes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either the control function or hereditary-information role.

modelAnswer: The nucleus is surrounded by a nuclear membrane.
It contains nucleoplasm and one or more nucleoli.
It also contains chromosomes, which are made of chromatin when the cell is not dividing.
Chromosomes contain DNA and genes that carry hereditary information.
The nucleus controls the activities of the cell.

items.followUp: Define enzymes and explain how temperature and substrate specificity affect their action.

rubric.why: Defines enzymes by their catalytic role in living organisms.
rubric.description: Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed up chemical reactions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining an enzyme as a biological catalyst.

rubric.why: States the protein nature of enzymes.
rubric.description: Most enzymes are proteins.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that enzymes are proteins.

rubric.why: Describes the specificity of enzyme action.
rubric.description: An enzyme acts on a particular substrate or catalyses a particular reaction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing enzyme specificity.

rubric.why: Gives a further characteristic of enzymes.
rubric.description: Enzymes are reusable because they remain unchanged after a reaction; their activity is affected by temperature and pH, and extreme conditions can denature them.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct characteristic such as reusability or the effect of temperature or pH.

modelAnswer: Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed up chemical reactions in living organisms.
Most enzymes are proteins.
Each enzyme is specific to a particular substrate or reaction.
An enzyme remains unchanged after a reaction and can be used again; its activity is affected by temperature and pH, and extreme conditions can denature it.
